priceSnapshot.note: THE EVENT CLEARED, THE MACRO TURNED, AND BITCOIN BARELY MOVED. That sentence is the whole report. June core PCE landed at 3.3% y/y against 3.3% consensus with the monthly rate cooling to +0.1% from +0.3%, headline 3.7% in line - the binary print that capped morning's confidence resolved benign. What followed was a broad risk-on repricing: the dollar index is 100.068, down 0.81% and at a six-week low, QQQ is +3.08% at $682.10, JPXN is +3.96%, gold +0.75%, silver +1.37%, copper +2.28%, and the 10-year held steady at 4.68%. A falling dollar with stable yields is the friendliest macro combination BTC has had all week. Against that, BTC is up 0.19% on the morning snapshot. It DID spike to 65,152.4 at 16:29Z and it DID force out $865,601 of shorts in the 65,000-65,250 band doing it - but it gave the entire move back inside forty minutes, printing 64,608.8 by 17:41Z and taking $149,073 of longs with it on the way down. That is a two-way flush, not a trend. Price now sits at 64,941.6 with the DAILY EMA50 at 64,948.82 - within nine dollars. Confidence rises 5.75 to 6.00 because the event risk is gone and the 4H MACD line has crossed above zero for the first time in this sequence; it does not rise further because an asset that cannot hold a breakout on a +3% Nasdaq day with a six-week-low dollar is telling you something about its own bid.

reduceIf.confirmation: A 4H CLOSE below $63,000 still confirms the structural range break. The rail is carried unchanged into a seventh consecutive session and has still never fired: the lowest print since the morning handover is 64,608.8 and the lowest since the rail was first set is 62,684. The tighter, non-structural line is $64,330 - that is the 4H EMA20 (64,329.54) sitting almost exactly on the 15m EMA200 (64,329.59). A 4H close back under $64,330 does not trigger the structural reduce; it simply cancels the long setup and sends the reserved cash back to the sidelines.

addIf.confirmation: The retest bid moves UP from morning's $64,400, because the market never traded there - the low was 64,608.8. The live shelf is $64,610-$64,750: that is where $149,073 of LONG liquidations were forced out between 17:38Z and 17:41Z, which means the weak longs on that shelf have already been cleared and what is left underneath is real bids rather than leverage. A 1H close holding above $64,700 is where the reserved cash goes to work. The separate momentum tranche is unchanged and still has not fired: a 4H CLOSE above $65,000 opens the thin air toward 65,373 and 65,727, and no 4H candle has closed above $65,000 yet - the 12:00Z candle closed 64,719.1 and the one in progress is at 64,941.6.

decisionBox.changed: Stance moves TAKE_PROFIT -> ADD. Confidence 5.75 -> 6.00. Probabilities 34/44/22 -> 35/45/20. What changed since 07:00 COT, in order of importance: (1) THE PRINT CLEARED. Core PCE came in at 3.3% y/y on consensus with the monthly rate halving to +0.1%, and morning explicitly sold a slice of spot to buy optionality across exactly this event. The event resolved favourably, so the correct use of that optionality is to put the cash back to work - that is the entire reason the stance flips. (2) THE MACRO REGIME IMPROVED MEASURABLY: DXY 100.068 at a six-week low, -0.81%; QQQ +3.08%; JPXN +3.96%; US10Y steady at 4.68%; Brent -1.01% at 89.82. (3) STRUCTURE IMPROVED: the 4H MACD line crossed ABOVE ZERO at +6.80 from -102.88 at the morning snapshot, with the histogram at +131.38, and price is above all four 4H EMAs. (4) AGAINST ALL OF THAT, BTC UNDERPERFORMED BADLY - +0.19% versus the Nasdaq's +3.08% - and the 65,152.4 spike was fully retraced in forty minutes. So the add is deliberately PARTIAL: roughly 45% of free cash goes in here, the rest waits for the $64,610-$64,750 shelf. Morning's own $64,400 retest bid never filled and the wallet still holds 31.27 USDT of idle cash, which is the thing this session has to fix without chasing. The $63,000 reduce rail and the $61,900 resting stop are both carried unchanged.

This is the pivot: held, it is the launchpad for a second run at 65,152; lost, it hands the tape back to the shelf below.

liquidityMagnet.note: Pull is UP, but it is a weaker up than morning's and the honest case against it should be read first. FOR: shorts were liquidated 6-to-1 over longs, and the long/short ACCOUNT ratio has fallen again from 1.40 to 1.26 while price rose - a third consecutive session of accounts leaning less long into strength, now the least crowded reading in four days. Funding is near flat (+0.00726% current period, perp premium -0.0498%), so nothing here is leveraged euphoria. AGAINST: the $865K of short fuel above was spent in a single four-minute burst and price could not hold the level it bought, and for the first time this week there is a real long-side flush underneath at $64,500-$64,750. The 1.26 ratio also cuts both ways - it is much closer to neutral than the 1.58-1.81 readings of the past two days, which means there are simply fewer trapped shorts left to squeeze. Treat $64,875 and $65,125 as the two edges of the same coin: whichever gives way first sets the afternoon.

calibration.note: Morning gets a clean mark, with one honest miss. Its ANALYSIS was right on every branch it named: it called the pull UP and price made a higher high at 65,152.4; it flagged the 15m RSI at 75.82 as the most stretched reading in 54 hours and momentum duly cooled to 58.98; it identified core PCE as the binary that would decide the session and the print landed benign at 3.3% on consensus. Its ACTION - selling roughly 12% of the spot core at 64,821.4 to restore dry powder ahead of that print - cost almost nothing and bought exactly the optionality it was supposed to: price is only $120 above the sale four hours later, so the round trip on that slice is about 0.19%, and the event it was hedging resolved in the wallet's favour. Its MISS is that the $64,250-$64,450 retest bid it set never filled - the low was 64,608.8, $160 above the top of the band - so the cash it freed sat idle for the whole session. That is a sizing-of-the-bid error rather than a directional one, and the fix is in this report: the add trigger moves up to the $64,610-$64,750 shelf where the market actually traded and where longs were actually flushed.
